headline: Managing High Demand at Lake Louise and Moraine Lake
reservation: A Parks Canada Discovery Pass is required for entry to Banff National Park. Due to high demand, access to the lakeshores often requires advanced booking for the official Parks Canada shuttle or a commercial provider; Moraine Lake is closed to personal vehicles. Systems change seasonally, so verify current booking windows on the Parks Canada website before planning.

days.title: Glacial Peaks and High Alpine Vistas
days.start: Suggested: 7:30 AM from Banff or Lake Louise Village

stops.name: Fairview Lookout
stops.detail: Hike the steep trail for an elevated perspective of the historic Fairmont Chateau Lake Louise and the Victoria Glacier.

stops.name: Lake Agnes Teahouse
stops.detail: Ascend the forested path past Mirror Lake to reach this seasonal alpine cabin nestled by a mountain tarn.

days.driving: Allow 45–60 minutes between Banff and the lake; conditions vary with shuttle timing.
days.note: Uphill hiking trails are rocky and can remain snow-covered well into June.

days.title: The Valley of the Ten Peaks
days.start: Suggested: 8:00 AM from the Park and Ride Lot

stops.name: Rockpile Trail
stops.detail: Climb the short, stony path at Moraine Lake for the quintessential view of the azure water and surrounding summits.

stops.name: Larch Valley
stops.detail: Follow the switchbacks through dense forest to reach open meadows that glow gold during the autumn transition.

days.driving: Shuttle transfers take roughly 20–30 minutes; allow for queue times.
days.note: This area is high-density grizzly bear habitat; check official group-size requirements for hiking.

days.title: Bow Valley Parkway Exploration
days.start: Suggested: 9:00 AM from Lake Louise Village

stops.name: Johnston Canyon
stops.detail: Walk the suspended catwalks to view the Lower and Upper Falls carved into the limestone canyon.

stops.name: Castle Mountain Lookout
stops.detail: Stop at the viewpoint for a panoramic look at the fortress-like peaks of the Sawback Range.

days.driving: Allow 1.5 hours for the scenic route to Banff; conditions vary by wildlife activity.
days.note: Seasonal road closures may apply to sections of the Bow Valley Parkway to protect local wildlife.

intel.title: Shuttle Priority
intel.text: The Lake Louise Drive area is subject to significant traffic management. Utilizing the official shuttle from the Trans-Canada Highway intercept lot is the primary way to visit both major lakes in one day.

intel.title: Early Starts
intel.text: Shuttle reservations typically open months in advance with a small portion released rollingly. Arriving at the Park and Ride early is essential regardless of your ticket time.

intel.title: Village Constraints
intel.text: Parking in Lake Louise Village is limited to short-term retail use. It is not a viable staging area for all-day hiking at the lakeshore.

intel.title: Connectivity Gaps
intel.text: Cellular service is generally reliable in the village but drops off significantly on the higher alpine trails. Download offline maps before leaving your accommodation.

intel.title: Last Service Points
intel.text: Fuel is available in Lake Louise Village and the town of Banff. There are no refueling stations along the Icefields Parkway heading north until Saskatchewan River Crossing.

plan.arrival: Collect your vehicle at Calgary International Airport and drive 2 hours west to Banff or Canmore to stock up on groceries before continuing to the lake area.
plan.vehicle: Standard vehicles are suitable for the main highways, while RVs may face restricted parking in the village and must use designated lots.
plan.goldenHour: Moraine Lake Rockpile provides iconic light at sunrise, though seasonal road closures limit access to summer and early autumn.
